scope_note: Third-pass modeled synthesis for NYSE Group's U.S. Liquidity Center in Mahwah. Three 2025 parcel-levy allocations use certified recipient rates that reconcile exactly to the direct parcel bill; a same-account break-even identity states the public-cost decision threshold without estimating cost or net benefit. A wide 28 MW utilization sensitivity exposes the theoretical annual site-electricity scale, a four-quarter WIPP conversion preserves parcel and period limits, and a zero-leave 24x7 support-coverage equivalent remains location-unallocated. All estimates are modeled_not_observed_or_audited and excluded from direct-record totals.

estimates.label: Annual same-account public-cost break-even threshold

period.label: Tax year 2025, complete block 139 lot 4 paid parcel charges

scope.label: All recipient jurisdictions represented in the 2025 NYSE/ICE-linked block 139 lot 4 consolidated parcel payment

interval.interpretation: Exact threshold identity over the cited paid account, not an estimate of actual cost.

parameters.name: parcel_property_tax_paid

provenance.detail: Four 2025 WIPP installments marked Paid with zero balance

parameters.transformation: Sets the equal-cost threshold for the same parcel account and recipient scope

estimates.confidence_rationale: The paid-account threshold is exact, while actual same-recipient marginal costs, incentives and economic incidence are unobserved.
estimates.decision_relevance: Makes the fiscal decision rule explicit: a positive margin requires all matched 2025 marginal public-service, infrastructure and incentive costs to be below $2,169,540; a negative margin requires them to exceed it.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Same-year marginal police, fire, road, administration, utility, infrastructure and incentive costs allocated across the same school, municipal and county recipients

derivation.formula: annual matched public cost at break-even = 2025 block 139 lot 4 property tax paid
assumptions: The threshold covers the same parcel account, tax year and recipient jurisdictions as the direct payment.
Actual marginal public-service, infrastructure and incentive costs are not inferred.
No positive or negative fiscal result is asserted.

limitations: Not an estimate of actual public cost or net benefit.
Payer and economic incidence are unresolved.
The parcel is not allocated to the original building and recipient cash timing is unavailable.
estimates.notes: Decision threshold only. No positive or negative net fiscal result is asserted.

estimates.label: Annual total-site electricity utilization sensitivity

period.label: Full-year theoretical sensitivity from the 2024 operator specification; not observed 2024 use

scope.label: U.S. Liquidity Center total-site 28 MW nameplate; customer and operator loads unallocated

interval.interpretation: Low, central and high annualize 25%, 50% and 100% average loading of the 28 MW total-site nameplate. The 100% case is a mathematical ceiling under continuous full-nameplate operation, not a forecast or true bound on metered use.

parameters.name: total_site_electrical_power
parameters.transformation: Convert to kW and multiply by annual hours and utilization

estimates.confidence_rationale: Only the 28 MW total-site nameplate is observed. Average loading, meter boundary, usable capacity, redundancy, outages and customer/operator allocation are unknown.
estimates.decision_relevance: Quantifies the order-of-magnitude and hard arithmetic ceiling implied by the published site rating while showing how strongly annual energy depends on utilization.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Interval-metered electricity, utility bills, peak demand, load factor, usable versus redundant capacity, outages, tariff determinants, and customer/operator allocation

derivation.formula: 28 MW total-site power × utilization × 1,000 kW/MW × 8,760 hours
assumptions: Utilization scenarios are 25%, 50% and 100% of total-site nameplate.
The model annualizes a non-leap year.
No PUE is applied because the source describes total-site electrical power rather than IT capacity.

limitations: Not actual, forecast or audited electricity use.
The 100% endpoint is a mathematical nameplate ceiling, not evidence of continuous full load.
No cost, emissions, water, economic output or tenant allocation is inferred.
estimates.notes: Wide nameplate-utilization sensitivity only; do not present as metered consumption or IT load.

estimates.label: Zero-leave minimum 24x7 Data Center Operations support coverage

period.label: Conditional annual coverage equivalent from the 2025 Mahwah operating policy

scope.label: One simultaneously covered Data Center Operations support post for Mahwah incidents; work location, onsite status and employment relationship unallocated

interval.interpretation: Mathematical zero-leave lower bound conditional on one continuously covered support post; not observed employee headcount or a claim that staff are onsite.

provenance.detail: Section 3.10 says the Data Center Operations team handling Mahwah colocation incidents is available on a 24x7 basis
Forty scheduled hours per week for 52 weeks, with zero leave, training, breaks, overlap or relief allowance

estimates.confidence_rationale: The role-specific 24x7 availability is directly stated, but one simultaneous post, physical work location, onsite status, employer or contractor, actual headcount and schedules are not reported.
estimates.decision_relevance: Provides a conservative labor-capacity floor implied by a documented continuously available Mahwah support function without relabeling it as facility employees or local jobs.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Actual support posts and headcount, physical work location, onsite status, employer or contractor, schedules, relief coverage, occupations, payroll and worker residence

assumptions: At least one Data Center Operations support post is continuously covered for the documented 24x7 availability.
One zero-leave FTE-equivalent supplies 2,080 scheduled hours per year.
No relief factor, job multiplier or onsite assumption is applied.

limitations: FTE-equivalent coverage is not employee headcount, filled jobs or payroll.
The source does not say support personnel are onsite or located in Bergen County.
Real coverage requires breaks, leave and relief, so actual labor supporting one post would exceed this zero-leave floor.
No wage, residence, contractor, supplier or household effect is inferred.
estimates.notes: Conditional support-coverage floor only; do not count as observed Mahwah employment.

estimates.label: Unit-converted rolling four-quarter municipal water withdrawal

period.label: Four consecutive quarterly bills due 2025-11-01 through 2026-08-01; rolling interval, not calendar year

scope.label: Mahwah WIPP water account 203167-0 for block 139 lot 4; parcel infrastructure and building allocation unresolved

interval.interpretation: Exact sum and unit conversion of four displayed quarterly usage fields; not an audited calendar-year or facility-only total.

provenance.detail: Township rate sheet denominates actual water usage in cubic feet and charges excess tiers per 100 cubic feet

parameters.name: gallons_per_cubic_foot
parameters.transformation: Convert cubic feet to U.S. gallons

estimates.confidence_rationale: The WIPP account fields and Township billing unit support the arithmetic, but exact service-date bounds, meter completeness, parcel sharing and selected-building allocation are unresolved.
estimates.decision_relevance: Provides the only bounded municipal resource quantity found and preserves its rolling-period and parcel-account limitations.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Exact meter service dates, all-meter completeness, original-building allocation, consumption versus withdrawal, wastewater discharge, cooling use, and audited calendar-year data

assumptions: The four consecutive portal usage fields use the Township's cubic-foot water billing unit.
The four rows describe consecutive quarters on the same account.
The value is not re-scaled to a calendar year or allocated between buildings.

limitations: Rolling four-quarter withdrawal is not calendar-year consumption or wastewater discharge.
The account is parcel-scoped and may include shared infrastructure or later development.
The portal does not establish meter completeness or exact service-period endpoints.
estimates.notes: Source-account sum and unit conversion; not facility-only or audited annual use.
